name: Bill Monahan

bio.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Monahan says he has lived in Tigard since 1982, served as Planning Director until 1988 and as City Manager from 1994 to 2005.
bio.excerpt: I have lived in Tigard since 1982, serving as Planning Director until 1988 and City Manager from 1994 to 2005.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

bio.statement: The pamphlet lists his prior government experience as Tigard City Manager and Community Development Director, Milwaukie City Manager and Brockton, Massachusetts City Planner.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Tigard – City Manager, Community Development Director Milwaukie – City Manager Brockton, MA – City Planner

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

bio.statement: Monahan's pamphlet statement lists his occupation as consultant, with 30 years in city government and work as an attorney.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Consultant Occupational Background: 30 years in city government; attorney; consultant

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Monahan says in his pamphlet statement that the police need a better facility but that city leaders must be more transparent and honest.
positions.excerpt: The police need a better facility, but city leaders must be more transparent and honest.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: In a May 2026 KATU report on the $150 million bond, Monahan said the project could be reduced in size and that police could be addressed first rather than in a combined facility.
positions.excerpt: I don't think it needs to be a combined facility. I think it can be split and police can be sought first.

positions.statement: Monahan's pamphlet statement lists delivering affordable core services among his priorities if elected.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Monahan's pamphlet statement lists leading with integrity, transparency and accountability, and building relationships with Council, staff and the community, as priorities.
positions.excerpt: Lead with integrity, transparency, and accountability

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: In May 2026 KATU coverage, Monahan said too much of the bond's cost was placed on residential properties.
positions.excerpt: I think there's too much being placed on the residential properties,
